```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2,
  out.width = "100%",
  cache.extra = packageVersion("interactmeta")
)
```

This article follows [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html). For **Bayesian**
CAMS fits, `traceplot()` draws **bayesmeta** Rubin-style diagnostics on
the stored native `bmr` / `bayesmeta` objects (interaction block and
combined-population block). There is no separate per-subgroup traceplot:
those coordinates are not separate meta-analyses under the CAMS
factorization.

```{r setup, cache = TRUE}
library(interactmeta)
library(metafor)

steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events, bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events, di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = steroids
)
des <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "Non-IMV")
fit <- cams(
  des,
  reference = "Non-IMV",
  tau.prior = function(tau) bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau, scale = 0.5),
  tau.interaction.prior = function(tau) bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau, scale = 0.1)
)
```

## Interaction block

```{r trace-int, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
traceplot(fit, type = "interaction")
```

## Combined block

```{r trace-comb, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
traceplot(fit, type = "combined")
```

See [`vignette("trial-specific-effects-and-shrinkage")`](trial-specific-effects-and-shrinkage.html)
for how shrinkage enters forest plots.
